messages:
Maya (People Ops): Heads up — new hire Samir Patel (remote, CA) has a background check flag: name on county court record is a partial match. I scheduled an I-9 session for Day 1 assuming in-person, but Samir is remote and asked for guidance. @Jon can you confirm if Samir can come on-site for ID verification?
Jon (Hiring Manager): He said he can't travel first week. Would prefer remote orientation. Any options?
Maya (People Ops): We can do a remote alternative under the Remote I-9 exception if the manager sponsors a notary or uses an authorized agent, or we can do an in-person verification later within 3 days. Need to resolve the BG flag first — sometimes it's OK if it's an old sealed record.
bg-check-bot: Background check status: REVIEW_REQUIRED — criminal record partial name match detected. Document: https://bg.example.com/reports/SMR-87231
Ruth (Security): If there's a record, we need the adjudication notes before final offer. @Maya is this already escalated to background adjudication?
Maya (People Ops): Not yet — filing now. @Luis can you take the adjudication intake? I'll pause the I-9 until we confirm.
Luis (People Ops): Taking it. Asked vendor for supporting docs from Samir (aliases, DOB confirmation). Sent email 10:14am.
Ezra (IT): On the I-9 front, if we do remote verification and use an authorized agent, make sure the agent signs the physical I-9 and we capture a scanned copy into Workday. For badging, we can provision a temporary virtual badge but physical building access requires verification at kiosk.
Jon (Hiring Manager): OK — I can ask Samir for scanned government ID and also to schedule a local notary. Would that satisfy Security?
Ruth (Security): Potentially. We'll need: scanned front/back of government ID, a scan of social security card or W-2 for name consistency, and the adjudication note from the vendor. If the records match and adjudicator says no concern, we clear and proceed.
Maya (People Ops): To help Samir, I sent him the remote I-9 checklist: https://handbook.redwood.com/hr/remote-i9-checklist — includes wording for the notary and the allowed agent form. Also pasted below the quick template he can show to the notary:
```
I, Samir Patel, authorize Notary/Agent Name to act as my authorized agent on behalf of Redwood Inference for I-9 documentation on DATE. Agent must attach a copy of their ID and sign Section 3 per USCIS guidance.
```
Jon (Hiring Manager): I'll forward that and ask for times. If adjudication takes >48h, do we delay start or onboard with limited access?
Maya (People Ops): We can still onboard them for non-sensitive systems and issue a provisional account with no production credentials. Security will block access until cleared. I'll coordinate provisioning notes with @Ezra.
Ezra (IT): Got it — I can set up a provisional SSO flag and restrict group membership. Send me the start date and the final clearance.
Luis (People Ops): Vendor responded — asked Samir to provide court disposition docs if available. Sending vendor case ID to Ruth and Maya.
Ruth (Security): Thanks. If we get the disposition showing no conviction, we clear. If there is one that impacts role, we'll loop in legal and hiring.
Jon (Hiring Manager): Thanks team. I'll message Samir now. Update me when adjudication done and I'll confirm his orientation schedule. :thumbsup:
Maya (People Ops): Thanks — filing thread notes here for audit. Will update BG status once vendor responds. :white_check_mark:
bg-check-bot: Background check status updated: AWAITING_CANDIDATE_DOCS (2025-11-07 10:27)
